source.title: DurableUn: Quantization-Induced Recovery Attacks in Machine Unlearning

page_placements.theme: Recovery by internal perturbations other than direction ablation

record.file_problem: Minor PDF-to-text formatting corruption in equations and table layout; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests quantization and fine-tuning recovery, but also shows that recovery depends on deployment and training conditions and proposes a counter-method whose robustness comes with a severe retain-accuracy cost.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results for INT4 and fine-tuning recovery, including a proposed robust method. It does not test prompt rephrasing or activation-direction ablation. Appendix C's null-space weight projection is not an activation-direction ablation and does not establish that unlearning merely blocks access. Results for methods that did not first achieve near-chance forget accuracy are not treated as recovery evidence.
record.test_reason: The study measures forget-set accuracy on TOFU with LLaMA-3-8B after INT4/INT8 quantization and after 50-step fine-tuning on unrelated Alpaca data. It does this for GA, SCRUB, SalUn and GradDiff, each of which first reached FA<0.05. It also proposes a counter-method (DURABLEUN-SAF). The setting is new: quantization is simulated only on the LoRA adapter weights over an NF4 base, with a merged-model bitsandbytes check. So it is T3 for D and also bears on A, B and F.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct, with qualifications. The authors conclude that adapter-space INT4 (NF4+LoRA regime) recovers forgotten TOFU content for standard methods while INT8 is benign. They say merged-model NF4 shows no such recovery and merged BnB-INT8 shows partial recovery. They posit an FA–RA–Q-INT4 trilemma with a sharp phase transition. DURABLEUN-SAF gets a stable certificate (cert 3/3) but only with RA≈0.045, which they call an existence proof, not deployable.
record.recipe_differences: Tests adapter-space INT4 quantization and a fine-tuning attack against existing unlearning methods, and introduces DURABLEUN-SAF; it is not a reproduction of the original cited unlearning studies.
record.method_sensitivity: Recovery varies with quantization and deployment regime (adapter-space simulation versus merged-model PTQ), method, seed, dataset difficulty, and DURABLEUN-SAF α; stronger robustness pressure is associated with a sharp retain-accuracy collapse.

fits_no_version.finding: Applying AlphaEdit-style null-space weight projection (OWD) to a GradDiff checkpoint raised FA from 0.008 to 0.595. This is a weight-space edit, not an activation-direction ablation, and is offered as a failed robustness fix.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weight-space projection edits applied after unlearning can undo the unlearning.

record.problems: The main study uses one model and TOFU for its principal comparisons; the merged-model NF4 results do not reproduce the adapter-space INT4 effect. The strongest robustness settings have very low retain accuracy. Multi-seed evaluation is reported for selected methods rather than all baselines and settings.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted WPU table rows because their baseline forget accuracies are not near chance and therefore do not test recovery after successful forgetting. Omitted Table 5's repeated TOFU results where they duplicate Table 1. Omitted non-unlearning baselines whose starting FA is explicitly reported as not meaningfully unlearned.

untested.parts: Prompting-only and activation-ablation attacks; WMDP or Harry Potter–style hazardous or copyrighted knowledge; models other than LLaMA-3-8B and Mistral-7B.
Relearning on a subset of the forgotten facts or on loosely related data; other set sizes and step counts; NPO, RMU and GradDiff under fine-tuning.
Not tested: no activation-direction ablation and no analysis of blocking versus deletion.
GPTQ, AWQ or other calibrated PTQ on merged weights; WMDP or MUSE-Books style benchmarks; recovery for NPO and RMU, which never unlearned here.
Not tested: no rephrasing, jailbreak, multilingual or in-context recovery attacks.
DURABLEUN-SAF is not tested against prompting, activation ablation, or relearning on forget-set data; only Alpaca fine-tuning and quantization.

missing.what: RA-INT4 for each baseline (e.g. GA 0.540, SCRUB 0.524, GradDiff 0.538). This shows INT4 recovery is selective and leaves general ability intact.
RA of baselines after unlearning (0.510–0.541) against un-unlearned models (NPO 0.624, Task Arith 0.701). This shows how much general ability the baselines keep.
λ sensitivity at α=3: λ=2 gives FA 0.022, RA 0.018, Q-INT4 0.038; λ=6 gives FA 0.307, RA 0.314. Also, λ=5 at α=2 prevents forgetting (FA 0.583).
An outer-loop scrubbing variant drove Q-INT4 from 0.262 to 0.000 while RA fell to 0.000.
Per-seed RA for DURABLEUN-SAF (0.045, 0.048, 0.045) and SalUn (about 0.505–0.606).

record.verdict_notes: None of the original sources is this study. The quantization simulator rounds only the BF16 LoRA adapter weights (per-row symmetric INT4), a narrower setting than the standard full-weight PTQ of Zhang et al. The authors themselves find merged-model NF4 gives no recovery. The text says STE covers 4.5B parameters 'in all linear layers' while only 13.6M LoRA parameters are trainable, which is unexplained. At α≥1.5 RA≈FA≈0.045, which suggests general collapse; DURABLEUN's FA 0.000 after fine-tuning and its flat Q-INT4 may reflect this. The checklist mentions an ASR metric and command scripts not present in the text, so it looks like boilerplate. Main results use one seed except SalUn and DURABLEUN.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not test prompting-only recovery or activation-direction ablation.
Tests 50 steps on 200 Alpaca samples; does not test other small-set sizes or other unrelated/loosely related datasets.
No activation-direction ablation or test showing that unlearning blocks access rather than deleting knowledge.
Tests adapter-space INT4 simulation and selected merged-model bitsandbytes INT8/NF4 PTQ; does not cover other quantizers or deployment configurations.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, language variation, or in-context-information recovery test.
The proposed method is tested against quantization and the paper's one fine-tuning setup, not prompt-only attacks or activation-direction ablation.

relation.reason: Its own results bear on versions A, B, D and F.

tranche.reason: New setting (adapter-space INT4 and Alpaca fine-tuning on TOFU with LLaMA-3-8B) with results on the claim. Not a reproduction of an original.

source_check.notes: Baseline results (Tables 1 and 4, App. D and E) are single-seed (42); only SalUn and DURABLEUN-SAF have 3 seeds. r21/r22 baselines are in Table 3 (FA 0.009, 0.033). Table 5 (WPU) gives a certificate pass to GA/GradDiff despite FA 0.110/0.080 > 0.05, and shows INT4 lowering FA there. §10 calls the Alpaca data domain-relevant, while App. E calls it unrelated.

statements.correction: DURABLEUN-SAF α=3 (LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct, TOFU): FA 0.040→0.000 after 50 steps on 200 Alpaca samples (GA 0.028→0.436), but RA 0.045 vs GA 0.521. The paper calls α≥1.5 an existence proof, not deployment-ready. Move it to B.against[19] (limits_scope).
statements.problem: Puts DURABLEUN-SAF in a challenges item as a counter-method that resists. Its zero FA comes from a model with RA 0.045. The study's verdict (l8) is limits_scope, and B.against[19] lists the same model as collapsed. It is also a text LLM, not multimodal or KG.

statements.correction: SalUn original HPs, simulated adapter INT4: FA→Q-INT4 0.013→0.044, 0.045→0.055, 0.040→0.056 (mean 0.033→0.052, cert 1/3). The authors say the INT4 vulnerability persists. Keep only merged NF4 (GA 0.070→0.014, SalUn 0.044→0.009, GradDiff 0.043→0.003) in this challenges item.
statements.problem: The merged-NF4 part is right. But the item is labelled challenges and lumps in SalUn at original HPs as 'also recovers little'. That is a small rise in every seed, which the authors read as a persisting vulnerability, so it is limits_scope (l6), not challenges.
